entry.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests. We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting.
entry.summary:
We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #cryptography #networking

entry.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Signing and Verification Performance of Verifiable Credential Formats: A Cross-Language Benchmark of SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM, and mdoc
entry.summary:
We compare the signing and verification performance of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats--SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5)--over one scope: issue, present with selective disclosure, verify. Node.js, Go and Python implementations ran in four environments, one a cloud VM (N=2,000 across five runs; medians of each statistic and the spread). For an end-to-end exchange disclosing 5 of 20 attributes, the total (issue, present, verify) on Node.js in the cloud VM is 0.265 ms for mdoc, 0.298 ms for SD-JWT VC and 0.534 ms for W3C VCDM.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography

entry.title: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption.
entry.summary:
Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time is spent on the number theoretic transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT), which reduce the complexity of polynomial multiplication from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #neuroscience

entry.title: O2N2: Efficient Doubly Oblivious Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
entry.summary:
Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search allows clients to search from an untrusted server without revealing sensitive queries, and is useful in scenarios like medical diagnostics and credit scoring. Among the various privacy-preserving primitives, trusted execution environments (TEEs) have much lower overhead than heavy cryptographic ones, yet they leak memory access patterns, enabling adversaries to infer query contents. Oblivious RAM (ORAM) can be used to hide those access patterns at $\mathrm{O}(\log N)$ asymptotic cost, but existing high-performance ANN search algorithms (e.g., IVF or HNSW) exhibit complex, data-dependent access patterns that are unfriendly for ORAM.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #databases

entry.title: Optimizing Two-Step Primal LWE Attacks with PnJBKZ Simulation
entry.summary:
Learning with Errors (LWE) and its variants underlie many lattice-based cryptosystems, making accurate concrete attack-cost estimates important for parameter selection. Practical primal attacks combine lattice-basis reduction with a final shortest-vector search, and their performance depends strongly on how these components are scheduled. We formalize the two-step strategy space considered in this work and propose PSSearch, a pruning-based method that selects a minimum estimated cost strategy under a specified reduction simulator and cost model.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Exploring Fault Injection Attacks on HQC and BIKE Beyond Fujisaki-Okamoto Verification
entry.summary:
Fault injection attacks have been extensively studied in the context of post-quantum cryptography, yet existing analyses on code-based KEMs largely focus on faults targeting the Fujisaki-Okamoto transform. This work presents new fault injection attacks against BIKE and HQC that operate beyond this commonly protected component and target less obvious instructions within the decapsulation process. The proposed attacks achieve full key recovery using only valid ciphertexts under NIST Level 1 parameters, requiring 17392 and approximately 3 million decapsulation queries for HQC and BIKE, respectively.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: On the Inapplicability of Residue-Confined Error Attacks to CRT-FHE with Non-Degenerate Error Distributions
entry.summary:
This paper responds to the cryptanalysis presented in “Key Recovery from Residue- Confined Errors in the Pradhan CRT-RLWE Construction” (Olejnik and Naskrecki, 2026), which claims key recovery and plaintext recovery against the CRT-FHE scheme introduced in “A New CRT-based Fully Homomorphic Encryption” (Pradhan et al., 2026). We demonstrate that the reported recovery attacks rely entirely on a deliberately con- structed error distribution whose support lies in the kernel of the CRT encoding function. Consequently, the effective encryption error is identically zero, reducing the attacked con- struction to a noiseless RLWE instance.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Exact SVP and CVP in Structured Lattices: Polynomial-Space Algorithms and Reductions
entry.summary:
Although module lattices possess richer algebraic structure than general lattices, their algorithmic benefits for exact shortest and closest vector problems (SVP and CVP) remain relatively unexplored. For general $N$-dimensional lattices, the fastest known polynomial-space algorithms take $N^{\Theta(N)}$ time, whereas known $2^{O(N)}$-time algorithms require exponential space. We investigate how the algebraic structure of modules over number fields can be exploited to obtain faster exact algorithms in polynomial space.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #infosec

entry.title: BBB Secure Large-Tweak TBC from Ideal Block Ciphers. At FSE'15, Mennink introduced the concept of designing beyond-birthday bound secure tweakable block cipher from an ideal block cipher.
entry.summary:
At FSE'15, Mennink introduced the concept of designing beyond-birthday bound secure tweakable block cipher from an ideal block cipher. They proposed two tweakable block ciphers $\widetilde{F}[1]$ and $\widetilde{F}[2]$ that accept $n$-bit tweaks using a block cipher with an $n$-bit key and $n$-bit data. Mennink proved that the constructions achieve security up to $2^{2n/3}$ and $2^n$ queries, respectively, assuming the underlying block cipher is ideal.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
